@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1MNYFW81216M57PS9NDZKBE
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: 8a80
+title: 'config show and config path: make the invisible configuration visible'
+---
+## What
+
+cli-plan.md §5.11. Nothing is on disk after an install, so the
+configuration is invisible today. These two commands show it. They add
+no setting: they read the stack of §5.10.
+
+In `Sources/acp-agent/ConfigCommands.swift`:
+
+**`config show`** prints the merged configuration as YAML to stdout.
+
+- `--source` annotates each key with the layer that set it: `builtin`,
+  `user` or `project`. `LayeredYAMLDocument` already returns source data
+  for each key, so this reads what the loader knows.
+- `--json` prints the same tree as JSON.
+- It honors `--cwd`, because `--cwd` selects which stack to read.
+- It prints every configuration warning to stderr, not to stdout.
+
+**`config path`** prints each layer path, one per line, with a mark for
+the ones that exist:
+
+```
+builtin  (in code, no file)
+user     /Users/x/.config/acp-agent/            exists
+project  /Users/x/repo/.acp-agent/              missing
+```
+
+`config show --source` is the important one. It answers "which layer won
+this value", which is the question a person actually has, and nothing
+answers it today.
+
+- [ ] `config show`, and `--source` and `--json`
+- [ ] `config path`, with the exists mark
+- [ ] Both honor `--cwd`
+- [ ] Warnings to stderr, report to stdout
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] With no file in any layer, `config show` prints the builtin
+      defaults, and `--source` marks every key `builtin`.
+- [ ] With a project `config.yaml` that sets one key, `--source` marks
+      that key `project` and the others `builtin`.
+- [ ] `config show --json` parses as JSON, and it holds the same values.
+- [ ] `config path` names three layers, and its exists marks are right.
+- [ ] Both exit 0, and both write their report to stdout.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ConfigShowTests.swift`: a
+      two-layer fixture — a user `config.yaml` and a project one that
+      overrides one key — asserts the merged values and the per-key
+      source.
+- [ ] The `--json` output decodes and equals the YAML output's values.
+- [ ] `ConfigPathTests`: with a temporary stack where only the project
+      layer exists, the output marks user missing and project exists.
+- [ ] A test asserts that a configuration warning goes to stderr and
+      never to stdout.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
